sanskrit:
न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः।
यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते।।
image_english: It is impossible to give up all activities. He who renounces the fruits is truly renounced.
caption:
Chapter 18, Verse 11

The biological reality. ‘na hi deha-bhṛtā śakyaṁ tyaktuṁ karmāṇy aśeṣataḥ’ (It is indeed impossible for an embodied being to give up all activities). ‘yas tu karma-phala-tyāgī sa tyāgīty abhidhīyate’ (But he who renounces the results of his work is called one who has truly renounced). You have to breathe, eat, and sleep. So total ‘Sannyāsa’ (stopping action) is a myth. The only practical definition of a Tyāgī is one who gives up the *fruit*. This validates Karma-yoga as the practical application of Sannyāsa.
